title: P5-09: Copy the real data (22 tables, 10.6 GB of S3, vector index) to the new backend and prove fidelity
description:
## Goal
The real data of the old backend is copied to the new backend, and an automated fidelity check proves it equal. Old data is not modified.

## Context (FACT, read-only 2026-10-07, old main backend AppSync s4sclnevjjbzpmj4vhallzvw3e, 39 tables)
- Rows (scan COUNT): SemanticNode 771, Assignment 395, CategoryKeyword 391, AssignmentEvent 413, Message 213, Reference 202, KnowledgeImportRun 199, KnowledgeArtifact 175, MessageThread 99, ProcedureRun 75, Category 46, SemanticRelationType 38, ReferenceAttachment 33, NewsroomSection 23, ProcedureDefinition 8, ProcedureVersion 8, KnowledgeCorpus 3, UserIdentity 3, UserRoleAssignment 3, CategorySet 2, UserProfile 2, SemanticRelation 1. All other tables (including Item, PublishedItem, Edition, PublishedEdition, EditionItem, Tag, ItemTag, MediaAsset, PublishedMediaAsset) are 0: THE NEWSPAPER HAS NO ARTICLES TO MIGRATE, so `convert-bodies` does not apply.
- Codex-branch backend (hfkkuckznzc47ch3ffcs2joy2m): all 39 tables 0 rows, pool us-east-1_GxxvFqQTQ 0 users: nothing to migrate; retired in P5-12.
- S3 media bucket `amplify-dbsyytcm9drqa-mai-papyrusmediabucket0dab24-4hstaautjdqo`: 53,183 objects, 10,606,928,317 bytes: `corpora/` 45,188 objects 10.5 GB (ai-ml-history, ai-ml-journalism, ai-ml-research in two letter cases, knowledge-index, and `pilobol-us/`, a misplaced Pilobolus prefix per the site-hosting anti-pattern), `newsroom/` 7,884 (payloads), `media/` 75 (38 MB), `inbound-email-archived/` 29, `inbound-email/` 7.
- S3 Vectors: bucket `...papyrusknowledgevectorbu-62gho8vanqsa`, index `papyrus-knowledge`.
- TI plans a generic one-off copy tool (PPY-301b12 context, "P4-08 one-off content copy tool (old backend to new)"). Reuse it; extend only if it does not cover these models. UserIdentity, UserProfile, UserRoleAssignment are excluded (new Cognito subjects, Q6).

## Exact steps
1. Dry run of the copy tool against the new backend: per-model counts, no writes.
2. Ryan yes: apply with the authoring role. Order: KnowledgeCorpus, CategorySet, Category, CategoryKeyword, NewsroomSection, Procedure*, KnowledgeArtifact, Reference, Semantic*, Assignment*, MessageThread, Message. Idempotent (re-run = zero changes).
3. `aws s3 sync` bucket to bucket (same region) for `corpora/`, `newsroom/`, `media/`, `inbound-email-archived/`; `corpora/pilobol-us/` is skipped (belongs to Pilobol.us, confirm with Ryan).
4. S3 Vectors: rebuild the index in the new backend from KnowledgeArtifact with the existing knowledge-index command (if the embedding cost is acceptable, state it first), else copy vectors with `list-vectors` and `put-vectors`.
5. Write the result table into this ticket.

## Acceptance checks
- Row count per model equals the list above (except the three user models, which are 0); checksum of row JSON excluding createdAt, updatedAt, owner and identity fields equal old vs new for every model.
- S3: object count and total bytes per prefix equal; key plus size manifest equal; 50 random objects byte-compared.
- Vector index: vector count equals the old index (or the re-embed count equals KnowledgeArtifact chunks, recorded), and 5 sample queries return the same top-3 ids old vs new.
- Re-run apply reports zero changes. Old backend row counts unchanged before and after.

## Rollback
New backend only: Ryan deletes the copied rows/objects or the new stack and redeploys empty. The old backend is read-only throughout.

## Risks
Writes between copy and cutover are lost: freeze editing in the old /newsroom during P5-09 to P5-11 (two to four editors, announce) and run a delta copy at cutover; cross-owner fields; copy tool gaps; sync time (about 10.6 GB, estimate under an hour).

## Needs Ryan
Yes for the apply (data writes), the corpora/pilobol-us decision, the freeze.

comments.text:
## Data-copy plan (read-only investigation 2026-10-09; nothing was written to either account; sub-task PPY-66408d created and set as blocker of this ticket)

### 0. CORRECTION to the ticket facts (re-counted today with `dynamodb scan --select COUNT` per table of the live API s4sclnevjjbzpmj4vhallzvw3e, paginated to the end)
The 2026-10-07 counts were low for four tables. Real counts (target = 0 rows everywhere, 39 tables, schemas identical): SemanticNode 10115 (not 771), Reference 6143 (not 202), ReferenceAttachment 5030 (not 33), Message 3472 (not 213), AssignmentEvent 413, Assignment 395, CategoryKeyword 391, KnowledgeImportRun 199, KnowledgeArtifact 175, MessageThread 99, ProcedureRun 75, Category 46, SemanticRelationType 38, NewsroomSection 23, ProcedureDefinition 8, ProcedureVersion 8, KnowledgeCorpus 3, CategorySet 2, SemanticRelation 1 = 26,636 rows to copy; identity tables not copied: UserIdentity 3, UserRoleAssignment 3, UserProfile 2. Total 26,644. The acceptance counts of this ticket must be replaced by these.
Live backend = stack amplify-dbsyytcm9drqa-main-branch-cb38ada667 (AppSync s4sclnevjjbzpmj4vhallzvw3e, pool us-east-1_40Uot7WSv). `amplify-dbsyytcm9drqa-main` does not exist; the codex stack is the empty one. Newest row write per table: Message/MessageThread 2026-08-26, ProcedureRun 2026-07-26, everything else 2026-07-04 or older (mostly May to 3 June). Nothing has been written for six weeks.

### 1. Inventory
S3 media bucket (source, SSE-S3, no versioning): 53,183 objects, 10,606,928,317 bytes (unchanged since 10-07). corpora/ 45,188 / 10,547 MB (AI-ML-research 40,411 / 10,347 MB; AI-ML-journalism 1,303 / 71 MB; AI-ML-history 432 / 39 MB; ai-ml-research 2,773 / 82 MB; ai-ml-journalism 168 / 4.5 MB; ai-ml-history 28 / 1.8 MB; knowledge-index 2 / 2.1 MB; pilobol-us 69 / 0.13 MB), newsroom/ 7,884 / 20.8 MB, media/ 75 / 38 MB, inbound-email-archived/ 29, inbound-email/ 7. 51,681 objects are under 1 MB; 197 are 8 MiB or larger (largest 203 MB); 116 have multipart ETags and all 116 are 8 MiB-part uploads. Target bucket amplify-ds6yswxui41yi-mai-papyrusmediabucket0dab24-uuzzq2kfc5vq: 0 objects, SSE-S3. Copy set (skip corpora/pilobol-us/ and inbound-email/): 53,107 objects, 10,606,772,143 bytes; skipped 76 objects, 156,174 bytes. No row in Reference, ReferenceAttachment, KnowledgeArtifact, KnowledgeCorpus or Message refers to corpora/pilobol-us/ (checked), so skipping it loses nothing.
S3 Vectors: source bucket ...papyrusknowledgevectorbu-62gho8vanqsa has two indexes. Live = `papyrus-knowledge` (1536, cosine, float32, 9,810 vectors: 8,434 reference-passage + 1,376 reference-summary; non-filterable metadata summary, sourceUri, text, title; the knowledge-query Lambda env points to it, model text-embedding-3-small). `papyrus-knowledge-e5-v1` (1024 dims, 9,810 vectors) is an unused experiment: NOT copied. Target: bucket ...papyrusknowledgevectorbu-u8bnh8rrlslz, index `papyrus-knowledge-p-apyr-us` already exists, 1536 cosine float32, same non-filterable keys, 0 vectors, and its query Lambda uses the same model/dimensions (OPENAI_API_KEY present).
Other state: EventBridge (source): rule rate(15 minutes) inbound-email processor (ENABLED) and an S3 Object Created rule on inbound-email/ to the SES receive Lambda; no other schedules or ingestion jobs; DynamoDB-stream triggers on Message: Slack delivery and console responder Lambdas (source only; the target has no event source mappings, so copying Messages into it triggers nothing). Source SES active rule set papyrus-inbound-p-apyr-us (MX stays on legacy until P5-11). SSM names (source main): GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, PAPYRUS_JWT_SECRET, PAPYRUS_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, PAPYRUS_SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET; no Secrets Manager secrets; backup plan PapyrusStorageBackupPlan exists on the source. Target SSM: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET and /papyrus/p-apyr-us/revalidate-secret; target EventBridge has the same two inbound-email rules (15-minute processor ENABLED): do not copy inbound-email/ into the target or its processor will ingest the 7 raw mails (Ryan: confirm those 7 are disposable; they are listed by key, not content).

### 2. Tool gap (read src/papyrus_content on origin/develop)
copy-backend takes `--source-outputs/--target-outputs` but signs every AppSync call with one process-wide credential chain (graphql_http._aws_credentials), resolves `stack:` and builds S3 clients from the ambient chain, and copies objects with `client.copy` using the TARGET client (needs read on the source bucket; cross-account is denied without a source bucket policy). Apply also copies objects one at a time. Same-account Threat Intelligence never hit this. Sub-task PPY-66408d "P5-09a: copy-backend: separate source/target credentials" (blocks this ticket): `--source-profile/--target-profile`, `--expect-source-account/--expect-target-account`, `--s3-transfer auto|server-side|stream` (stream = GET from the source session, PUT with the target session, preserving content type/metadata; single PUT for plain-MD5 sources and 8 MiB multipart for multipart sources so ETags reproduce), `--s3-workers N`, source session read-only, Gherkin first, docs updated. Also verified read-only: the admin SSO session can call both AppSync APIs (list query returns 3 corpora on the source, 0 on the target); whether it can WRITE to the target is only known at apply time; fallback is the target role p-apyr-us-papyrus-authoring (trusts the prod account root; needs a local AWS profile with role_arn, set up by Ryan).
Schema check (introspection of both APIs, 19 models to copy): identical fields, no required target field missing in the source, no enum value the target rejects: expect 0 invalid rows. Known limit: createdAt on the target is the copy time (updatedAt kept only where the model declares it); fidelity hashes exclude both.

### 3. S3 strategy
A) Stream through this Mac with two sessions (RECOMMENDED). No change to legacy, no local disk (disk has about 8 GB free; objects are streamed), SSO-only. Measured read-only: 100 MB ranged GET of the largest object = 12 MB/s with 8 threads (96 Mbps), 200 HEAD requests = 287 req/s with 32 threads. Estimate: bandwidth floor 10.6 GB / 12 MB/s = 15 min down; upload is usually the slower side, so 30 to 60 min total with 16 workers (51.6k small objects add 6 to 9 min of request time). Cost about $1.3: legacy data transfer out 10.6 GB x $0.09 = $0.95 (free if the account still has free-tier transfer), 53k PUT $0.27, 53k GET $0.02. Needs the sub-task tool change. Risks: SSO expiry or Mac sleep mid-run (re-run is idempotent; use caffeinate).
B) Bucket policy on the LEGACY bucket granting the prod principal read (server-side CopyObject, same region, no transfer charge, about 5 to 10 min, about $0.3). It is a WRITE to a live legacy production bucket and needs Ryan's explicit yes. Exact statement to append (the existing Deny non-TLS and CDK/SES statements stay): `{"Sid":"PapyrusProdMigrationReadOnly","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"<the prod principal ARN that runs the copy>"},"Action":["s3:GetObject","s3:GetObjectTagging"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::amplify-dbsyytcm9drqa-mai-papyrusmediabucket0dab24-4hstaautjdqo/corpora/*","arn:aws:s3:::amplify-dbsyytcm9drqa-mai-papyrusmediabucket0dab24-4hstaautjdqo/newsroom/*","arn:aws:s3:::amplify-dbsyytcm9drqa-mai-papyrusmediabucket0dab24-4hstaautjdqo/media/*","arn:aws:s3:::amplify-dbsyytcm9drqa-mai-papyrusmediabucket0dab24-4hstaautjdqo/inbound-email-archived/*"]}` plus `{"Sid":"PapyrusProdMigrationList","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{...same...},"Action":"s3:ListBucket","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::amplify-dbsyytcm9drqa-mai-papyrusmediabucket0dab24-4hstaautjdqo"}`. Rollback: save `get-bucket-policy` output first and `put-bucket-policy` it back (the policy is CDK-managed, so any later pipeline deploy also reverts it; drift risk if forgotten). The tool would still need the sub-task for per-side AppSync credentials, so B saves only S3 time.
C) `aws s3 sync` with a role chain: one CLI process has one credential set, so it needs B's policy or a new IAM role in legacy (also a legacy write) or local staging of 10.6 GB (disk does not allow). Rejected.
D) S3 Batch Operations / Replication: needs the source bucket policy plus job role, or versioning on the source for replication (a bigger legacy change). Overkill for a one-off. Rejected.
Recommendation: A. Use B only if Ryan wants the wall time cut from about 45 to about 8 minutes and says yes.

### 4. Vector index
There is an existing rebuild path: `python -m papyrus_newsroom knowledge-vector-index --action sync|rebuild|audit` (src/papyrus_knowledge_query/vector_index.py; deterministic keys; derives from accepted References, their extracted text in corpora/, and insight Messages; embeds with OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, needs OPENAI_API_KEY; target selected by PAPYRUS_S3_VECTOR_INDEX_ARN). Embedding cost would be about $0.05 (9,810 vectors x about 250 tokens), but the result is not guaranteed bit-identical or the same count (current chunking/accepted set vs the 2026-05 index). Recommendation: COPY the 9,810 vectors of `papyrus-knowledge` into `papyrus-knowledge-p-apyr-us` (exact, free, about 3 min, no OpenAI key), then run `knowledge-vector-index --action audit` against the target (read-only) as the semantic cross-check, and keep `sync` as the delta tool. A copy is a one-off boto3 script in the scratchpad (no repo change): list_vectors (1000 per page) then get_vectors (100 keys per call, returnData and returnMetadata) from the legacy session, put_vectors (500 per call) with the prod session, same keys; re-run overwrites with identical content. Metadata holds corpus text: never print it.

### 5. Order of operations (every command asserts `aws sts get-caller-identity` per profile first; legacy 335163751677, papyrus-production 712236451410)
P0 prerequisites: PPY-66408d released and pinned; P5-07/P5-08 done (target exists: yes, UPDATE_COMPLETE); SSO sessions for both profiles (Ryan).
P1 baseline (read-only): counts, S3 manifest, vector count; keep in a scratch dir outside the repo. (Done today: the numbers above.)
P2 DRY RUN (read-only, review with Ryan), with S=stack:amplify-dbsyytcm9drqa-main-branch-cb38ada667 and T=stack:amplify-ds6yswxui41yi-main-branch-23e5d23a59:
`papyrus ops content copy-backend --source-outputs $S --target-outputs $T --source-profile legacy --target-profile papyrus-production --expect-source-account 335163751677 --expect-target-account 712236451410 --models KnowledgeCorpus,CategorySet,Category,CategoryKeyword,NewsroomSection,ProcedureDefinition,ProcedureVersion,ProcedureRun,KnowledgeArtifact,KnowledgeImportRun,Reference,ReferenceAttachment,SemanticRelationType,SemanticNode,SemanticRelation,Assignment,AssignmentEvent,MessageThread,Message --s3-prefixes corpora/AI-ML-history/,corpora/AI-ML-journalism/,corpora/AI-ML-research/,corpora/ai-ml-history/,corpora/ai-ml-journalism/,corpora/ai-ml-research/,corpora/knowledge-index/,newsroom/,media/,inbound-email-archived/ --manifest-dir <scratch>/dry --json > plan.json`
Expected output (the read-only equivalent I could do today): all 19 models create = the counts in section 0, 0 update, 0 invalid, target 0 rows; 3 identity models skipped; S3 53,107 objects / 10,606,772,143 bytes missing in the target, 76 skipped (pilobol-us 69, inbound-email 7), 0 target objects.
P3 Ryan: yes to the apply (writes in papyrus-production), the freeze, and the pilobol-us / inbound-email skips.
P4 Freeze: announce no editing in the old /newsroom (two to four editors). There are no scheduled jobs that write data except the 15-minute inbound-email processor, which only acts when mail arrives at submissions@ / suggestions@p.apyr.us (MX is still legacy); I do NOT disable it (that would be a legacy write): the cutover delta covers it.
P5 Apply rows: same command plus `--apply --s3-prefixes none --manifest-dir <scratch>/apply`. Sequential AppSync writes, 26,636 rows, estimate 20 to 45 min (reads about 1 min).
P6 Apply S3 (can run in parallel with P5): `... --models none-equivalent` is not supported, so run the same command with `--s3-prefixes <list above> --s3-transfer stream --s3-workers 16 --apply` after P5 or accept that it re-plans the rows as unchanged; estimate 30 to 60 min.
P7 Vectors: the copy script above (about 3 min), then the read-only audit.
P8 Fidelity: (a) re-run P5/P6 command: expect 0 create / 0 update / 0 copy; (b) diff `source/models/counts.json` vs `target/models/counts.json` (19 equal, 3 identity models 0 on the target) and the per-row `content-manifest.json` hashes (id by id); (c) `source/s3/keys.json` vs `target/s3/keys.json` (key and size equal for 53,107), per-prefix summary, ETags equal (including the 116 multipart objects); (d) 50 random objects byte-compared (sha256 of the streamed GET from both buckets, nothing on disk); (e) vector count 9,810 = 9,810, per-key sha256 of data+metadata equal, and 5 queries (use 5 stored vectors from different corpora as query vectors, so no OpenAI call) topK 3 returning the same keys and distances on both indexes; (f) source row counts and S3 count/bytes unchanged before/after (26,644 rows; 53,183 objects; 10,606,928,317 bytes).
P9 Write the result table into this ticket.
P10 Cutover delta (P5-11): after the freeze and before DNS/MX, repeat P5, P6, P7 (re-run is idempotent: only changed or new rows/objects move; vectors via the same script or `knowledge-vector-index --action sync` on the target) and P8.

### 6. Rollback
Nothing in the old backend is touched (source session is read-only; the source also has PapyrusStorageBackupPlan). Target: re-run is idempotent and the tool never deletes; to wipe, Ryan deletes the rows (batch delete per table), `aws s3 rm --recursive` on the target prefixes, and `delete-vectors` on the target index (the index itself is CDK-managed: keep it), or redeploys the target stack empty. Deletions are Ryan's.

### 7. Approvals needed from Ryan
1) Merge/release of PPY-66408d. 2) Yes to the apply (rows, S3, vectors written in papyrus-production 712236451410). 3) The edit freeze of the old /newsroom. 4) Confirm skipping inbound-email/ (7 raw mails) and corpora/pilobol-us/ (69; no row refers to it). 5) Do NOT use option B unless Ryan explicitly says yes (write to a legacy bucket policy). 6) If the admin SSO role is denied AppSync writes on the target: a local AWS profile for p-apyr-us-papyrus-authoring.

### 8. Risks
Ticket counts were wrong (updated here); SSO expiry or sleep (idempotent re-run, caffeinate); sequential row writes make the apply 20 to 45 min; stream mode must be written and tested (ETag reproduction relies on the 8 MiB-part finding); mail arriving in the window (delta); metadata contains corpus text (never print); total cost about $1.5 to $2.

Scratch manifests used for this investigation stay out of the repo and are deleted.
